nodes.name: History of Religion
nodes.description: The historical study of religious traditions, institutions, and change over time.

nodes.name: Theology
nodes.description: The systematic study of the divine and of religious doctrine from within a tradition.

nodes.name: Comparative Religion
nodes.description: The comparative study of the beliefs and practices of different religions.

nodes.name: Phenomenology of Religion
nodes.description: The descriptive study of religious experience and the sacred as they appear to believers.

nodes.name: Sociology of Religion
nodes.description: The study of religion as a social institution and its interaction with society.

nodes.name: Anthropology of Religion
nodes.description: The ethnographic study of religious belief, ritual, and symbolism across cultures.

nodes.name: Psychology of Religion
nodes.description: The study of religious experience, belief, and behavior through psychology.

nodes.name: History of Religion
nodes.description: The historical study of the development and transformation of religious traditions.

nodes.name: Ritual Studies
nodes.description: The interdisciplinary study of ritual action, performance, and meaning.

nodes.name: Study of Mysticism
nodes.description: The study of mystical experience and contemplative traditions across religions.

nodes.name: Religion and Science
nodes.description: The study of the relations between religious belief and scientific knowledge.

nodes.name: Christianity
nodes.description: The monotheistic religion centered on the life and teachings of Jesus Christ.

nodes.name: Islam
nodes.description: The monotheistic religion founded on the Qur'an and the teachings of Muhammad.

nodes.name: Judaism
nodes.description: The monotheistic religion and culture of the Jewish people rooted in the Torah.

nodes.name: Hinduism
nodes.description: The diverse family of religious traditions of the Indian subcontinent.

nodes.name: Buddhism
nodes.description: The religion founded on the Buddha's teaching of suffering and its cessation.

nodes.name: Sikhism
nodes.description: The monotheistic religion founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab.

nodes.name: Jainism
nodes.description: The Indian religion emphasizing non-violence and liberation from rebirth.

nodes.name: Zoroastrianism
nodes.description: The ancient Iranian religion founded on the teachings of Zarathustra.

nodes.name: East Asian Religions
nodes.description: The religious traditions of China and Japan, including Daoism and Shinto.

nodes.name: Indigenous Religions
nodes.description: The religious traditions of Indigenous peoples worldwide.

nodes.name: New Religious Movements
nodes.description: Religious movements that emerged in the modern era outside established traditions.

nodes.name: African Diaspora Religions
nodes.description: The religions formed by African-descended peoples in the Americas.

nodes.name: Ancient Religions
nodes.description: The religions of antiquity that no longer have living communities of practice.

nodes.name: Systematic Theology
nodes.description: The organized exposition of the doctrines of a faith as a coherent system.

nodes.name: Moral Theology
nodes.description: The theological study of moral action and the good life.

nodes.name: Biblical Theology
nodes.description: The theological interpretation of the Bible as a whole.

nodes.name: Liberation Theology
nodes.description: The theology that reads faith from the perspective of the poor and oppressed.

nodes.name: Feminist Theology
nodes.description: The theological critique and reconstruction of religious traditions from a feminist standpoint.

nodes.name: Secularization Studies
nodes.description: The study of the decline or transformation of religious authority in modernity.

nodes.name: Religion and Politics
nodes.description: The study of the interaction between religious communities and political life.

nodes.name: Catholicism
nodes.description: The Christian communion in union with the Bishop of Rome.

nodes.name: Eastern Orthodoxy
nodes.description: The Eastern Christian churches tracing continuity to the Byzantine tradition.

nodes.name: Oriental Orthodoxy
nodes.description: The ancient Eastern churches that separated after the Council of Chalcedon.

nodes.name: Protestantism
nodes.description: The Christian traditions originating in the sixteenth-century Reformation.

nodes.name: Anglicanism
nodes.description: The Christian tradition of the Church of England and its global communion.

nodes.name: Lutheranism
nodes.description: The Protestant tradition founded on the theology of Martin Luther.

nodes.name: Calvinism
nodes.description: The Reformed Protestant tradition following the theology of John Calvin.

nodes.name: Methodism
nodes.description: The Protestant movement originating in the revivals of John Wesley.

nodes.name: Pentecostalism
nodes.description: The charismatic Christian movement emphasizing the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

nodes.name: Sunni Islam
nodes.description: The largest branch of Islam, following the community and the sunna.

nodes.name: Shia Islam
nodes.description: The branch of Islam holding leadership of the community to descend through Ali.

nodes.name: Sufism
nodes.description: The mystical tradition of Islam seeking direct experience of God.

nodes.name: Ibadi Islam
nodes.description: A distinct early branch of Islam predominant in Oman and North Africa.

nodes.name: Islamic Law
nodes.description: The jurisprudence of Islam, including fiqh and sharia.

nodes.name: Quranic Studies
nodes.description: The scholarly study of the Qur'an's text, interpretation, and reception.

nodes.name: Hadith Studies
nodes.description: The study of the sayings and traditions of the Prophet Muhammad.

nodes.name: Orthodox Judaism
nodes.description: The Jewish tradition adhering to traditional interpretation of Jewish law.

nodes.name: Conservative Judaism
nodes.description: The Jewish movement balancing tradition with historical change.

nodes.name: Reform Judaism
nodes.description: The progressive Jewish movement adapting tradition to modern life.

nodes.name: Reconstructionist Judaism
nodes.description: The Jewish movement treating Judaism as an evolving civilization.

nodes.name: Kabbalah
nodes.description: The Jewish mystical tradition interpreting the nature of God and creation.

nodes.name: Rabbinic Judaism
nodes.description: The Judaism of the Talmud and rabbinic tradition after the Temple's destruction.

nodes.name: Vaishnavism
nodes.description: The Hindu tradition devoted to Vishnu and his incarnations.

nodes.name: Shaivism
nodes.description: The Hindu tradition devoted to Shiva as the supreme deity.

nodes.name: Shaktism
nodes.description: The Hindu tradition devoted to the Goddess in her many forms.

nodes.name: Smartism
nodes.description: The Hindu tradition that worships multiple deities as forms of one reality.

nodes.name: Bhakti Movement
nodes.description: The devotional Hindu movement centered on loving surrender to a personal deity.

nodes.name: Theravada
nodes.description: The Buddhism of South and Southeast Asia following the Pali canon.

nodes.name: Mahayana
nodes.description: The great vehicle of Buddhism dominant in East Asia emphasizing the bodhisattva ideal.

nodes.name: Vajrayana
nodes.description: The tantric Buddhism of Tibet and Mongolia emphasizing esoteric practice.

nodes.name: Zen
nodes.description: The Chan/Zen tradition of East Asian Buddhism centered on meditation.

nodes.name: Pure Land Buddhism
nodes.description: The Buddhist tradition focused on rebirth in the Pure Land of Amitabha.

nodes.name: Nichiren Buddhism
nodes.description: The Japanese Buddhist tradition based on the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.name: Tiantai Buddhism
nodes.description: The Chinese Buddhist school systematizing the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.name: Huayan Buddhism
nodes.description: The Chinese Buddhist school of the Avatamsaka Sutra and interpenetration.

nodes.name: Tibetan Buddhism
nodes.description: The Vajrayana Buddhism of Tibet and the Himalayas.

nodes.name: Dzogchen
nodes.description: The Great Perfection teaching of Tibetan Buddhism on innate awareness.

nodes.name: Digambara
nodes.description: The sky-clad Jain sect whose monks renounce all possessions.

nodes.name: Svetambara
nodes.description: The white-clad Jain sect that allows monks to wear simple robes.

nodes.name: Daoism
nodes.description: The organized Chinese religion of the Dao, with its pantheon, ritual, and alchemy.

nodes.name: Shinto
nodes.description: The indigenous religion of Japan centered on kami and shrine ritual.

nodes.name: Shamanism
nodes.description: The religious practice centered on shamans who mediate with the spirit world.

nodes.name: Animism
nodes.description: The attribution of spiritual agency to natural entities and objects.

nodes.name: African Traditional Religions
nodes.description: The indigenous religious systems of sub-Saharan Africa.

nodes.name: Yoruba Religion
nodes.description: The religion of the Yoruba people centered on the orisha.

nodes.name: Native American Religions
nodes.description: The diverse religious traditions of Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

nodes.name: Aboriginal Australian Religions
nodes.description: The religious traditions of Aboriginal Australians, including the Dreaming.

nodes.name: Polynesian Religions
nodes.description: The traditional religions of Polynesian peoples, including mana and tapu.

nodes.name: Baha'i Faith
nodes.description: The monotheistic religion founded by Baha'u'llah teaching the unity of humanity.

nodes.name: Mormonism
nodes.description: The Latter-day Saint movement founded by Joseph Smith.

nodes.name: Caodaism
nodes.description: The syncretic Vietnamese religion combining Buddhist, Daoist, and Christian elements.

nodes.name: Tenrikyo
nodes.description: The Japanese new religion founded on the revelations of Nakayama Miki.

nodes.name: Rastafari
nodes.description: The Afro-Caribbean religious movement centered on Haile Selassie and repatriation.

nodes.name: Vodou
nodes.description: The Haitian religion combining West African and Catholic elements.

nodes.name: Santeria
nodes.description: The Cuban religion of Yoruba origin devoted to the orisha.

nodes.name: Candomble
nodes.description: The Afro-Brazilian religion of Yoruba and Fon origin.

nodes.name: Mesopotamian Religion
nodes.description: The religion of Sumer, Babylon, and Assyria with its pantheon of city gods.

nodes.name: Ancient Egyptian Religion
nodes.description: The religion of pharaonic Egypt centered on the gods and the afterlife.

nodes.name: Ancient Greek Religion
nodes.description: The polytheistic religion of ancient Greece centered on the Olympian gods.

nodes.name: Norse Religion
nodes.description: The pre-Christian religion of the Norse peoples with its gods and myths.

nodes.name: Manichaeism
nodes.description: The dualistic religion founded by Mani that spread across Eurasia.
